nodes.recap: chapter header + arriving at the coastal town
nodes.text:
-------------------------------
|          CHAPTER 17          |
-------------------------------


$CThe night's rest is poor.# All of you say so in the morning,
around the fire Theo has built to cook breakfast,
without quite agreeing on why.##

$Y"I had bad dreams,"$C# Smiurl announces,
which is no surprise, because you did too, and you suspect everyone did.#
Efeliah says it is mental tension finding its outlet in sleep,
not real danger, probably, and looks at the town below with an expression
that does not entirely match what she is saying.##

The town sits in the bay like something washed ashore and left to rot:
an agglomeration of old wood, stacked hull-planks, inverted keels for rooftops,
a main gate that is simply a ship's prow set upright in the ground.
A vague, acrid smell carries up the hill on the sea wind.##

$c<<I have a bad feeling about this.#
Smiurl has already said this out loud.# I choose to keep mine internal.>>$C##

nodes.recap: entering the town - ominous quiet
nodes.text:
After about an hour you reach the main road bisecting the town,
and proceed in single file down the middle of it.##

Houses of rotted wood stand like relics of a forgotten age,
their windows nailed shut.# A faint stench of fish seeps through everything,
clinging to the walls and the air both.# There is no sound.#
Not the quiet of absence, but the quiet of waiting,
a watching silence that settles on your neck like a hand.##

Corolla has her hand on her blade.#
Smiurl's skin has gone a flat, unhappy ochre.##

Not one building stands intact.# Ruin has insinuated itself into every corner,
aided by time, and no gull cries.# You notice the absence of gulls
after a while, as a wrong note in a piece of music.##

You lead, and you walk, and nothing dares break the silence but your own footsteps.##

nodes.recap: the building - Frankenstein construction, they go inside
nodes.text:
On the right: a building three stories tall: wood, but not the rotted wood
of everything else around it.# Still standing, or at least maintaining
the pretense of standing, constructed from boards of different origins,
nailed together with the logic of someone who had six ships' worth of timber
and a single axe and a great deal of time.##

A ship's tiller hangs above the entrance like an amputated limb.##

The door is ajar.# From inside comes the flicker of firelight.##

You had caught what might have been movement inside, at the corner of your eye,
watching from the left-hand side of the street.# You approach the entrance,
under a crooked portico, and a fetid smell of fish is stronger here.##

$c<<I am walking into a building in an abandoned port town
that smells of fish and is built from cannibalized ships.#
This will probably be fine.>>$C##

You take the handle and push the door open.# You go in first,
and the others follow.##

nodes.recap: inside the building - the bar, the chandelier, the dark porticos
nodes.text:
The room inside is large and quadrangular, high-ceilinged,
and dark in the way that a great deal of firelight paradoxically creates darkness
beyond its own reach.# From the center of the ceiling hangs what appears to be
a chandelier made of bone, or at least of something that may have been bone,
hung with dozens of candles that do little against the shadows pooled
in the colonnaded porticos running around all four walls.# A shaft of light
falls obliquely from a skylight in the upper level and disappears into the dark above.##

Ahead of them, a raised bar counter occupies most of the far wall.##

They advance carefully between overturned chairs and ropes that coil
across the floor like sleeping snakes, watching the shadows,
until behind them, with a tremendous and sadistic creak, the door swings shut.##

The room goes darker.##

Kriss's hand is on his sword.# Only Efeliah seems, on the surface, calm.##

$g"We are not alone."$C##

Her thought barely has time to land before the porticos fill with light.
Tiny torches, dozens of them, crowding into every alcove on every floor,
and then their bearers swarm down from the shadows into the room around them.##

They are small, dwarf-small, dense, compact, and they are all old:#
wrinkled faces, vacant eyes, scalps cracked and browned by the sun,
bent backs, and on every face the same expression of consuming, irrational,
personally offended contempt for the people standing in their room.##

And then the worst one climbs onto the bar counter.##

He is perhaps the oldest, or the cruelest, or the ugliest,
or all three at once, the combination being greater than the sum of its parts.
Five others stand at his back on the counter.# He surveys your group
with tiny eyes the color of yellowed ice, lit from within by a lurid and
completely committed madness, and then he opens his mouth and says,
in a voice of terrible authority:##

$r"'Oukurtzen los.'"$C##

nodes.recap: Efeliah translates the tribunal - the party heckles, player picks when to draw steel

dialogues.precomment:
You look at the creature on the bar counter.#
Then at the several dozen gathered around you.
Then back at the creature.
dialogues.comment: You are uncertain whether to be afraid or simply offended.

dialogues.precomment: Efeliah's voice arrives in your mind, flat and composed.
dialogues.line:
It is a language none of you know.# I can read his thoughts.#
He is saying... that you have profaned and violated
the territory of the Edzzen.# That you are emissaries of, and I am rendering
this faithfully, 'the worthy-of-atrocious-sufferings-and-death,'#
or else enemy spies, or possibly ambassadors of distant kings.#
In any case you are condemned to die.

dialogues.comment: You say it, perhaps not quietly enough.
He says it without inflection, looking at the creature on the bar.

dialogues.precomment:
The creature on the counter does not appear to enjoy the interruption.
He fixes you all with a gaze of refined malice and continues,
his voice rising to a pitch of theatrical outrage.
dialogues.line:
He says...# you will die.# Today.#
They will eat your tongues,# and then hang you from the royal ship,#
and the fish will dispose of your putrid remains.

dialogues.precomment: Corolla studies the thing on the bar counter with an expression of pure contempt.
dialogues.line: He looks like a child's attempt to draw a corpse.
dialogues.comment: You cannot help it.# You laugh.##

dialogues.precomment: The creature's eyes bulge.# Efeliah relays his response without visible emotion.
dialogues.line:
He asks if you are laughing at your own end.#
He suggests that if so, you should die now.#
He is gesturing theatrically.

nodes.recap: the bar fight - one of them dives off the counter with a knife
nodes.text:
And then one of them leaps.##

It flings itself from the counter on a rope, a serrated knife catching
the candlelight as it swings toward you.# And you have the sword out
before you have consciously decided to draw it, pivoting on your heel,
using the flat of the blade like a bat.#
The creature cartwheels away with a shriek and hits the floor hard.##

You stand there with the sword in your hand, and in the bone-lit dimness
it is catching the light the way metal should not,
brightening and shifting impossibly, and you are looking at the thing
on the bar counter with eyes that are possibly on fire.#
Theo has reached behind his back for his hammers.#
Corolla has a blade in each hand.# Smiurl is somewhere above you.##

$c"Ef!# The door!"$C##

That is enough.# The whole room surges.##

encounter.victorymessage:
$CYou push through.#

Not cleanly, there is nothing clean about this, but the wave of them
breaks against the four of you long enough for Efeliah to wrench the door
open from its frame, and you pour through it into the street, running.#
Every blow is a body in your way; every body that falls is ground gained.#
Their howls fill the building and spill out into the alley beyond.##

You run.##
encounter.defeatmessage:
$CThe room swarms.# There are too many of them
and they are fast, faster than things their size should be,
and eventually the weight of numbers drags you down.##

The candlelight flickers above you.# Somewhere on the bar counter,
a dreadful old voice is pronouncing something terrible
and feeling very satisfied about it.##

nodes.recap: running through the town - the pursuit
nodes.text:
The street receives you at a run and gives you nothing to work with:
no clear direction, no cover, just more of the same warped wood
and nailed-shut windows, and the sound of the Edzzen pouring out of the building
behind you like something overflowing.##

They are fast.# Unpleasantly, disproportionately fast for their size,
scuttling between the buildings, spilling into the alleys ahead,
trying to flank and surround.# Smiurl is already at the front,
leaping in great panicked arcs over obstacles.##

$B"They'll take us!"$C##

$c<<Think.# Think.>>$C#

$g<<The ships!>>$C# Efeliah says in your head.# $g<<Theo!# The ships!>>$C#
Theo understands immediately, and changes direction.# Corolla, somehow,
also understands, and she turns and points:#

$R"Diversionary run.# Up there, the promontory!# Go!"$C##

$Y"Diversionary?!# Us?!"$C##

Smiurl has one half-second of pure anguish,
and then he is running after Corolla and you
because there is no third option and his legs have already decided.##

nodes.recap: lighthouse turn 1 (shared) - bar the ground floor door
nodes.text:
$CThe three of you spill into the base of the lighthouse and Smiurl slams the door
shut behind you with both hands, and for a moment you just stand there, breathing.##

The room is bare stone and old salt air, empty except for what the keepers left behind:
a coil of heavy rope, an iron mooring ring bolted into the wall beside the frame,
and a length of ship's timber leaning where someone propped it and forgot it.
A narrow slit window, barred with iron, looks out onto a wall of small, furious faces.##

Something hits the door hard enough to shudder the whole frame.##

Above you, past the door and the failing light, a spiral stair climbs into the dark.

actions.answer:
You wedge the timber through the iron ring and lash it fast with the rope,
Corolla throwing her whole weight against it as the door groans and holds.##

It will not hold forever.# Up the spiral stair, then, and no time to admire the work.

A coil of rope, an iron ring, a length of ship's timber, and a door
that is not going to hold on its own.# Outside, the wall of small furious faces
has not moved.# Whatever you do, do it now.

You hesitate half a second too long, weighing rope against ring against timber,
and in that half second the door takes a blow that splits one plank clean through.##

There is no time left to do this properly.# You shove Smiurl toward the stair instead.

nodes.recap: lighthouse turn 2 (fast) - climb the stair
nodes.text:
$CThe stair spirals up inside the lighthouse wall, steep, narrow, and dark,
and the noise from below follows you up it, muffled by the door but not gone.##

Somewhere above, Smiurl is already shouting something that might be encouragement.

actions.answer:
You climb, three steps at a time where the stair allows it, until it opens
into the lamp room at the top, dead glass on every side and Smiurl's voice close now.

Just stone steps curling upward, and behind you, muffled, the sound
of a door being generally disagreed with.
You slow, and somewhere below something heavy hits the floor.# That decides it.

nodes.recap: lighthouse turn 3 (fast) - lamp room, through the hatch
nodes.text:
$CThe lamp room is dead, glass on every side and the great lens dark and cold,
and there is no way out of it that you can see, until you hear Smiurl again,
his voice coming down through a hatch in the ceiling.##

$Y"Up here!# This way!"$C

actions.answer:
You haul yourself through the hatch after him, and the wind on the lighthouse roof
hits you like something solid, cold and full and entirely uninterested in your plans.##

Corolla comes up right behind you.

Glass walls, a dead lamp, and one hatch in the ceiling,
Smiurl's voice coming through it, not patiently.
You wait one second too many, and the stair behind you fills with the sound of feet.

nodes.recap: lighthouse turn 4 (fast) - wedge the hatch on the roof
nodes.text:
$CYou are on the roof now, railing on every side, the sea a long way down
in every direction.# Below you, through the hatch, the stair is still full
of noise, climbing toward you.##

Corolla has her stiletto out, waiting on you.

actions.answer:
Corolla jams the stiletto through the hatch's iron loop with one hard twist,
buying you seconds rather than safety, and you both know it.
The hatch, Corolla's stiletto, the railing, and a very long way down.
You hesitate, and the hatch bucks once under a fist from below.

nodes.recap: lighthouse turn 5 (fast) - spot the ship, jump
nodes.text:
$CThe wind is full and the light is terrible, and somewhere below,
the sea is doing whatever the sea does, entirely indifferent to all of this.

actions.answer:
You lean out over the seaward railing.# Far below, along the harbor wall,
a ship is moving parallel to the coast, sails immense and faintly luminous,
the largest of them tilted up toward the sun like a ramp.

condition.refusal: You don't even know what's down there yet. Look first.

actions.answer:
Two strides.# Your foot on the railing.# You go off the edge of the lighthouse
into the void, and you have exactly enough time to regret it before you don't.

Another crash below, and Corolla's hand finds your shoulder and simply shoves.#
You do not so much decide to jump as discover that you already have.

nodes.recap: fast path - Kriss lands on the ship, Corolla throws Smiurl, bigger Edzzen appears
nodes.text:
$CYou hit the sail flat and $Wslide$C, the great panel angled just right, a chute
of taut luminous material, and you come off the bottom of it and land heavily
on a mass of coiled ropes and furled canvas and what feels very much like a mattress.##

You lie there for one second and look up at the lighthouse, a very small tower
against the sky, then get to your feet.##

$c<<That actually worked.# I want to be very clear, to myself,
that I had no idea it would.>>$C##

Above you, on the roof: Corolla has turned from the railing.# Smiurl is still
crouched at the hatch, holding it, his skin a blinding white-yellow alarm,
and he has not noticed that you are gone.# Corolla walks to him, deliberate,
takes hold of him by the back of his jacket, and before he can finish the sentence
that begins with $Y"But what are you..."$C he is airborne.##

His scream cuts off when your hands catch him on the deck.##

Corolla takes her run-up toward the railing, and then she stops.##

A figure has pulled itself over the edge of the roof.##

Larger than the others.# Not by much, but enough to matter up here:#
broader in the shoulder, moving with a deliberation the small ones lack.
It draws two daggers from its belt with a grin that is possibly the worst
expression you have ever seen, and settles into a fighting crouch.##

Below, on the deck, the three of you look up.

nodes.recap: fast path - Corolla's rooftop duel, narrated - wound on the old burn scar

dialogues.precomment:
They circle each other along the lighthouse railing, high above the sea,
Corolla with a dagger out, the bigger Edzzen with two.#
The wind is full and the light is terrible and below,
on the deck, none of you can do a thing but watch.#

She feints right.# The Edzzen charges and she shifts left,
but his second blade catches her, a glancing blow across the back,
exactly where the Ayonn burn-scar sits.#

She cries out, a real cry, sharp, involuntary, and loses her balance,
going hard into the railing.# The dagger leaves her hand.##

Smiurl makes a sound beside you.##

She does not answer.# Above you, you see her grip the railing
with both hands, and her head drops for one second,
and the Edzzen is already moving toward her again.##

She does not have a weapon.# She has the railing.#
And she has the Edzzen's momentum.##

At the last instant she twists aside, and the Edzzen's face meets the railing with a crack
that carries all the way down to the deck.##

In the half-second the creature spends with its head against the metal,
Corolla takes her run, three steps on the open roof, hooks a foot
off the back of the Edzzen's shoulders and goes over the railing headfirst.##
dialogues.comment:
She hits the sail.##

She slides.##

She lands hard on the deck, harder than you did,
and she does not get up immediately.# She lies there, not moving,
while Smiurl and Efeliah are already crouching over her
and Theo is already casting off the mooring lines.##

The last thing visible on the lighthouse roof, above,
is the Edzzen's expression, a precise composition of bafflement and fury,
now surrounded by many of his colleagues, shrinking
as the ship carries you away from the promontory, into open water.##

nodes.recap: lighthouse turn 2 (slow) - climb the stair, door already failing
nodes.text:
$CThe stair spirals up into the dark, and behind you the ground floor door
is already losing the argument, one plank at a time.##

Smiurl's voice comes down from somewhere above, thin and urgent.

actions.answer:
You take the stair fast, badly, catching your shoulder twice on the curve
of the wall, until it opens into the lamp room and Smiurl's voice is suddenly close.

Stone steps, curling up into the dark, and behind you a door
that is not going to be a door for very much longer.

nodes.recap: lighthouse turn 3 (slow) - lamp room, through the hatch, pursuit closing
nodes.text:
$CThe lamp room is dead glass and a cold lens, and no way out you can see,
until Smiurl's voice finds you again, coming down through a hatch in the ceiling.##

$Y"Up here!# This way!# Hurry!"$C##

Somewhere below, on the stair, feet are climbing far too fast for anything
you would call reassuring.

actions.answer:
You haul yourself through the hatch and the wind hits you flat,
and Corolla comes up right behind you, already turning back toward the opening.

A dead lamp, glass on every side, one hatch, and feet on the stair
that are already closer than they should be.

nodes.recap: lighthouse turn 4 (slow) - wedge the hatch, no time left
nodes.text:
$CYou are on the roof, the sea a long way down on every side, and below
the hatch the stair has already gone from noise to something closer to a stampede.##

Corolla has her stiletto out.

actions.answer:
You jam it through the iron loop together, hurried, badly seated,
buying seconds you both know you do not really have.
The hatch, the stiletto, the railing, and no time to enjoy the view.

nodes.recap: slow path - the bigger Edzzen reaches the roof before anyone can jump
nodes.text:
$CYou have not even reached the seaward railing when you hear it:#
metal on metal, somewhere below the roof's edge, climbing the same steel bracing
that holds the lighthouse to the cliff.##

A hand finds the railing.# Then another.# And then it hauls itself up and over,
bigger than the others by enough to matter up here, broader in the shoulder,
moving with a deliberation the small ones lacked.# It draws two daggers
from its belt with a grin that is possibly the worst expression you have ever seen.##

$R"Kriss!"$C# Corolla shoves Smiurl behind her and reaches for her own blade,
but the thing is already between you and the railing, and between the railing
and the sea, and between the sea and anywhere you would rather be.##

There is no jumping past this one.

nodes.recap: slow path - Kriss fights the bigger Edzzen directly, tougher tuning
nodes.text:
$CYou draw the sword, and for once you are grateful for its unreasonable weight.##

The creature comes in low and fast, both daggers working, and you understand
in the first exchange that this is not the bar counter's swarm of angry old men.#
This one has done this before.

encounter.victorymessage:
$CIt goes down hard, daggers skittering across the stone, and does not get up.##

Corolla is already at the railing, pulling Smiurl to his feet, blood on her sleeve
where she caught a stray blade shielding him:# a shallow line across her back,
sitting exactly on the old burn scar from Ayonn.# She does not seem to have
noticed yet.##

$R"Later,"$C# she says, before you can ask.# $R"Jump."$C
encounter.defeatmessage:
$CYour arm gives a half-second before the rest of you does, and the last thing
you properly register is Corolla's voice, and then nothing at all.$d##


-- GAME OVER --#


$DThe universe just watched you lose a knife fight to a thousand-year-old dwarf.
It is not impressed.# Try again.

nodes.recap: slow path - post-fight escape, Corolla wounded, all three reach the ship
nodes.text:
$CCorolla does not wait for you to catch your breath.# She takes her run-up,
hooks Smiurl under one arm bodily, ignoring his indignant squawk, and goes over
the railing with him before you have entirely processed that the fight is over.##

You follow, because there is nothing else on this roof worth staying for.##

You hit the sail flat and $Wslide$C, the great panel angled just right,
and come off the bottom of it onto a mass of coiled rope and furled canvas
that only barely qualifies as a mattress.# Corolla lands beside you a moment later,
considerably less gracefully, Smiurl still clamped under one arm and shrieking about it.##

Only then, sitting up, does she notice the blood soaking through her sleeve,
and her face goes the color of the deck a half-second before the rest of her does.##

Efeliah is at her side before you can call out.##

Above you, the lighthouse and its remaining tenants shrink fast
as the ship pulls away from the promontory, into open water.

nodes.recap: end of chapter - away from the town, Corolla unconscious
nodes.text:
The lighthouse diminishes behind you, and the wretched town with it,
until the promontory is only a dark finger against the pale sky
and then the coast itself is only a line, and then only a suggestion,
and then gone.##

The sails above you are already angling toward the sun,
slowly, with a mechanical patience that seems almost affectionate,
and the motors engage below the waterline with a clean,
untroubled hum.##

Corolla has not woken up.##

Efeliah is beside her, and has not moved from beside her,
and Smiurl has arranged himself at a distance that is trying very hard
not to look like hovering.##

$c<<She got hit on the old burn scar.#
She'll be fine.# Corolla is always fine.#
I am saying this with full confidence and no anxiety whatsoever.>>$C##

$CTheo stands at the wheel.# Or rather near it, since the navigation computer
is already managing the course.# He looks at the panels above
with an expression you would describe, if pressed, as reverent.##
